title: Promote latch with telemetry-led checkpoints and graceful backout
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Introduce a promote-latch primitive that gates traffic promotion on telemetry-driven checkpoints and supports automated graceful backout. Adds observability and a rollback playbook for staged/AB rollouts.
description:
Summary: Adds a 'promote latch' primitive to the rollout runtime that enforces telemetry-driven checkpoints during canary/promote phases and wires an automated graceful backout playbook. Motivation: We've seen several incidents where a quick promote followed by a manual rollback caused session disruption and inconsistent user experience. This change makes promotion decision points explicit, observable, and abortable by the system when health signals deteriorate.

What this PR changes: Implements a latch state machine that can be attached to promotion plans. The latch evaluates a configurable set of telemetry checks (latency P95, error rate, semantic-regression signal from eval hooks, user-facing anomaly detector) at defined holdpoints. If thresholds are exceeded the latch triggers one of three actions: pause, slow-reduce-traffic, or backout. Backout is a graceful revert that preserves active session affinity and replays a small percentage of traffic to snapshot-mode for forensic capture.

Design details: - New API surface: rollout.spec.latches[] with 'checks', 'holdpoint_ms', 'action_on_violation' and 'grace_window_ms'. - Latch executor runs as part of promote coordinator (coord/promote_latch.go). It subscribes to the telemetry bus and evaluates windowed signals with exponential smoothing to avoid flapping. - Added a compact policy DSL for composite checks (e.g. "p95(latency, 60s) > 250ms and semantic_regression > 0.02"). - Backout path triggers a snapshot-and-drain flow: mark new model variant as draining, continue serving existing sessions for up-to 60s (configurable), persist recent requests to replay buffer for debugging, and reduce traffic fractions per-step to avoid sudden capacity shock. - Session affinity: when backout occurs we keep sticky sessions routed to the previous variant for their session TTL. That required plumbing session-cookie metadata through the swap plane.

Files touched (high level): - coord/promote_latch.go (new) - coord/latch_policy.go (new) - telemetry/telemetry_bus.go (mod) - controlplane/api/v1/rollout.proto (mod) - controlplane/server/rollout_handlers.go (mod) - runtime/drain_replay.go (new) - acceptance/e2e/promote_latch_test.go (new) - docs/rollouts/promote-latch.md (new)

Commits (summary): - Add promote latch state machine and executor - Add telemetry composite-check parser and evaluator - Wire latch into promote coordinator and API - Implement graceful backout drain + replay buffer - Unit + integration tests for latch + backout scenarios - Docs and rollout playbook

Testing done: - Unit tests for policy parser and executor: coverage for composite boolean expressions and time windows. - Integration e2e harness: simulate canary with injected latency/error, assert latch pauses promotion at configured holdpoints and triggers backout when condition persists. - Load test: 5k RPS synthetic traffic with model swap; verified no p95 regression during drain window. - Manual smoke: verified session stickiness preserved during backout in both hosted and dedicated modes.

Rollout plan: This is gated behind a feature flag rollout.promote_latch_enabled. Default remains off. Staged rollout plan: 1) Enable for internal org (1%) for 24h with verbose logging and wired smoke checks. 2) Increase to 10% after 48h if no backouts and health signals stable. 3) Expose to public customers as opt-in in Redwood Console.

Operational runbook (short): - Triggered when latch performs backout: check telemetry dashboard (new 'PromoteLatch' pane) for signals and recent decision trace. - If false positive: use 'resume' action to let coordinator re-evaluate after a manual holdpoint override. - For persisted replay buffer: run replay tool (scripts/replay_tool) against a staging cluster for reproduction. - For prolonged failures: revert feature flag and open incident with 'rollout-latch' tag.

Safety considerations: - To avoid noisy backouts, we use smoothed windows and require violation persistence > grace_window before backout. - Backout is conservative: we prefer pause or step-down traffic before full revert. - All decision traces are recorded and can be audited.

Related items: Linked Linear tasks ENG-1427 (promote latch design) and ENG-1433 (telemetry integration). This PR references prior incidents documented in INT-2041.

Why this is different from previous rollouts: Instead of ad-hoc holdpoints, this makes checkpoints first-class, pluggable, and machine-enforceable. The goal is to reduce manual intervention and make rollouts reproducible and auditable while reducing user-visible disruption during rollbacks.
review_conversation: Ethan Miller (reviewer) - 2025-10-24: Looks good overall. Two asks: 1) can we add a short-circuit to avoid latch evaluation for extremely short-lived canaries (< 5s), and 2) prefer using the existing tracing context rather than a new decision ID to keep logs correlated.
Priya Kapoor (author) - 2025-10-25: Added short-circuit for canaries under holdpoint_ms < 5000 in promote_latch.go. Kept decision_id but now embed trace_id when available; updated logs accordingly.
Aditi Rao (reviewer) - 2025-10-27: Tests look thorough. Minor nit: the policy DSL parsing should reject unhashed metric names to avoid accidental typos. Please add a validation step.
Priya Kapoor (author) - 2025-10-28: Added policy validation with a white-list of metric names (telemetry/allowed_metrics.go). Tests updated.
Miguel Santos (reviewer) - 2025-10-30: Approved on second pass. Verified e2e run locally and the backout drain respects session TTLs. CI flake in telemetry bus test fixed in last commit.
CI Bot - 2025-11-01: All checks passed on main CI after squash. Lint: pass, Unit: pass, Integration: pass, E2E: pass.
risk_assessment: Medium. The controlplane changes are additive and feature-flagged. The primary risk is incorrect policy expressions causing premature backouts; mitigated by validation and staged rollout. Load impact during drain was tested; documented capacity headroom required.
notes_for_release_eng: Enable behind rollout.promote_latch_enabled=false by default. Coordinate with SRE to add 'PromoteLatch' dashboard to canaries' standard view. Prepare replay infra for customers that enable automatic replay capture.
backout_playbook: 1) On violation, latch may: PAUSE -> REDUCE_TRAFFIC (step down by configured fractions) -> BACKOUT (drain + revert). 2) Backout preserves session affinity for TTL. 3) Decision traces and replay buffers are stored under /replays/<rollout-id>. 4) To restore: use server-side 'resume' or toggle feature flag off.
testing_guidance: Use acceptance/e2e/promote_latch_test.go; to simulate semantic regression attach eval-hook: /scripts/inject_semantic_regression --magnitude 0.03. For load, use perf/traffic_generator with session-cookie enabled to exercise affinity paths.
notes: Authored by Priya Kapoor (runtime team). This PR was demoed at the 2025-11-05 internal rollout guild meeting; slides attached in docs/rollouts/promote-latch.md.
